faq.q: What is the origin of Seydou?
faq.a: Seydou is associated with Arabic. Seydou is the West African (Fulani) form of Arabic سَيِّد (Sayyid), meaning 'master, lord'.
Yes — the underlying form سَيْدُو is Arabic.
Seydou can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Seydou should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Sayyid is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Seydou, seydou. Script forms are سيدو, سَيْدُو, سیدو, सेयदु.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
